params.name: p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph
params.convention: The sampling period of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard, 20 Hz (one scene every 50 ms): the step bound of headingSince, the largest gap between two consecutive scenes it integrates across; not a look-back window and not an action window.

params.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
params.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

params.name: p.yaw_rate_tolerance
params.convention: Yaw-rate resolution: the noise floor of a source's yaw-rate estimate, below which a heading is read as not changing.
params.source: Vehicle IMU and tracker yaw-rate noise figures.

params.name: p.caravan_entry_vehicle_length
params.convention: Overall length of the longest design combination a highway is designed for (an interstate semitrailer combination), so that any vehicle or combination can occupy the space.
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, WB-67 design vehicle overall length.

params.name: p.caravan_entry_time_headway
params.convention: Minimum accepted lead and lag time gap of a merging or lane-changing vehicle, applied once ahead of and once behind the entering vehicle.
params.source: Lane-change gap-acceptance studies (critical lead and lag gaps of about one second).

params.name: p.same_direction_cos_tolerance
params.convention: Heading alignment: cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same way of travel (about a quarter of a right angle), covering lane changes and road bends.
params.source: Lane-change trajectory geometry in naturalistic driving data.

params.name: p.straight_through_max_heading_change
params.convention: Turning-movement classification at a junction: a crossing whose net heading change stays below this bound is a through movement, not a turn.
params.source: Intersection turning-movement classification practice in trajectory studies.

params.name: p.against_direction_cos_tolerance
params.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which a heading still points against a carrier's designated direction (about half a right angle).
params.source: Wrong-way-driving detection practice (heading opposed to the lane direction beyond a cone).

params.name: p.turn_recognition_window
params.convention: The time within which a turn or a reversal, a reversal made in several moves included, is completed: the window over which the heading change that recognizes it is measured.
params.source: Intersection turning times and three-point-turn durations in naturalistic driving data.

params.name: p.left_turn_min_angle
params.convention: The heading change to the left beyond which a manoeuvre is a turn rather than a lane change or a bend's drift.
params.source: Turning-movement classification practice in trajectory studies.

params.name: p.reversal_min_angle
params.convention: The heading change magnitude from which the heading has come round to the opposite direction (a reversal); also the upper end of a left turn's band.
params.source: U-turn classification practice in trajectory studies.

params.name: p.reversal_max_angle
params.convention: The heading change magnitude beyond which the heading has come round past the opposite direction (a loop rather than a reversal).
params.source: U-turn classification practice in trajectory studies.

params.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
params.convention: Stop-point tolerance of the approach convention: the distance between a road user's body and the governing mark (stop line, crosswalk or intersection edge) within which a halt counts as made at that mark, set from the spread of halting positions at stop-controlled approaches.
params.source: Observational studies of stopping position at stop-controlled approaches (FHWA/ITE stop-sign compliance studies)

params.name: p.approach_view_sight_distance
params.convention: Sight distance along a crossing way that gives a view of approaching traffic: the stopping sight distance at a 30 mph design speed.
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance table

params.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
params.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
params.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

params.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
params.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

params.name: p.opposed_approach_cos_tolerance
params.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which two approach carriers' designated directions are still opposite directions (about 45 degrees), separating opposite approaches from crossing ones at junctions whose legs meet near right angles.
params.source: Intersection leg geometry convention (AASHTO Green Book: legs intersecting at angles near 90 degrees)

params.name: p.immediate_hazard_time_gap
params.convention: Critical gap of gap acceptance: an approaching vehicle whose time to reach the conflict (its distance over its speed) is at most this gap is an immediate hazard to a turning, crossing or merging manoeuvre.
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual, base critical headway (4.1 s for a major-street left turn)

params.name: p.yield_sign_check_speed
params.convention: Speed to which a vehicle at a yield-controlled approach slows so that it can still halt before the conflict (about 15 mph).
params.source: AASHTO Green Book intersection sight distance, Case C yield control (approach speed reduction)

params.name: p.obstruction_encounter_reach
params.convention: Distance between a pedestrian's body and an obstruction within which the pedestrian is at the obstruction (encountering it, or moving around it).
params.source: Pedestrian lateral clearance and shy distance (AASHTO Guide for the Planning, Design and Operation of Pedestrian Facilities)

params.name: p.pedestrian_detour_side_distance
params.convention: Largest distance between a detouring pedestrian's body and the sidewalk that is still as far to the side near the sidewalk as possible: one pedestrian width plus a shy distance from the curb.
params.source: AASHTO Pedestrian Guide: pedestrian space width (about 0.75 m) plus shy distance

params.name: p.sidewalk_return_time
params.convention: Time within which a pedestrian who has cleared an obstruction steps back onto the sidewalk: the walking time to cover a few metres at the design walking speed.
params.source: MUTCD pedestrian walking speed 3.5 ft/s (1.07 m/s)

params.name: p.overtaking_lateral_clearance
params.convention: Lateral clearance of the bicycle operating envelope: the shy distance between a bicyclist's body and a motor vehicle beside it below which the pass is close enough to endanger either.
params.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (bicyclist operating space and shy distance to motor vehicles, about 1 m).

params.name: p.right_turn_min_angle
params.convention: The heading change to the right beyond which a manoeuvre is a turn rather than a lane change or a bend's drift; the right-hand counterpart of the left-turn bound.
params.source: Turning-movement classification at junctions (FHWA Traffic Monitoring Guide turning-movement counts; the left-turn bound of this reading).

params.name: p.course_change_sin_tolerance
params.convention: Lane-change kinematics: the heading of a vehicle changing lanes or turning departs from the lane direction by about three degrees or more, a smaller departure being in-lane steering correction; the bound is the sine of that angle.
params.source: Naturalistic lane-change trajectory studies (heading-angle distributions of lane changes, e.g. Toledo and Zohar 2007; NGSIM lane-change analyses).

params.name: p.queue_standstill_gap
params.convention: Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it; car-following models put the jam gap at about 2 m and observed queues at signals reach about 4 m.
params.source: Intelligent Driver Model jam distance (Treiber, Hennecke and Helbing 2000) and field observations of standstill spacing at signalized intersections.

params.name: p.off_roadway_reach
params.convention: One standard lane width (12 ft): a shoulder separated from the vehicle's body by no more than one lane is reachable by one lateral move, and is beside the vehicle.
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (standard 12 ft travel lane).

params.name: p.free_passage_width
params.convention: Width a passing design vehicle needs: the 8.5 ft (2.6 m) design vehicle width plus a shy margin of about 0.4 m.
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (design vehicle dimensions).

params.name: p.perception_reaction_time
params.convention: Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from sighting a need to halt to applying the brakes, chosen to cover most drivers.
params.source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (Green Book), stopping sight distance

params.name: p.surface_friction_accel_dry
params.convention: Deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model, which most drivers achieve and most paved surfaces sustain when dry; also read as the acceleration a dry surface sustains in a bend.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance deceleration rate

params.name: p.surface_friction_accel_wet
params.convention: Deceleration a wet paved surface sustains: a wet-pavement friction coefficient of about a quarter at highway speeds, times gravity; also the acceleration it sustains in a bend.
params.source: Pavement skid-resistance data (AASHTO Guide for Pavement Friction)

params.name: p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow
params.convention: Deceleration an icy or snow-covered surface sustains: a friction coefficient of about a tenth, times gravity; also the acceleration it sustains in a bend.
params.source: Winter road friction measurements (PIARC Snow and Ice Databook)

params.name: p.following_min_time_headway
params.convention: Car-following: the smallest time gap to the road user ahead at which a following driver can still react to its braking; gaps below it are classed as close following.
params.source: Time-headway criteria of naturalistic driving and traffic-flow studies

params.name: p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed
params.convention: Time-to-line-crossing convention: drifting at a heading error of about one degree, a vehicle keeps at least one second before its body reaches the lane edge, so the free lateral margin it needs is its speed times the sine of that error times that time.
params.source: Godthelp, Milgram and Blaauw (1984), time-to-line-crossing

params.name: p.oncoming_cos_tolerance
params.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which another vehicle's heading still counts as oncoming: about forty-five degrees, which keeps vehicles meeting on a bend and excludes crossing traffic.
params.source: Geometric convention for opposing-direction classification (headings within a half right angle of opposed)

params.name: p.low_beam_seeing_distance
params.convention: Seeing distance of a low beam: the distance ahead within which a low beam reveals persons and vehicles, about 160 ft.
params.source: Driver handbooks (e.g. the Nevada DMV Driver Handbook) and IIHS headlight evaluations

declarations.meaning: The place of the observation lies within the territorial limits of an incorporated city.
The stretch of highway at the observation lies outside every territory classed as a business district.
The motor vehicles of the trace that travel one behind another in the same lane travel together as an organised caravan or motorcade.
The road user's current plan includes a right turn at the target region.
The road user's current plan includes a left turn at the target region.
A short section of the sidewalk on which the pedestrian is travelling is missing or cannot be passed on foot, at the place the pedestrian leaves it.
The area of the highway between the bicycle lane or path the pedestrian occupies and the adjacent sidewalk cannot be passed on foot at the observation.
The road user's vehicle is disabled: it cannot proceed under its own power at the observation.
The road user is engaged in the performance of official duties at the observation.
An emergency is in progress for the road user at the observation.
The school the zone serves is not in session on the day of the observation.
The observation falls in the period that begins a half hour after the school the zone serves last ceased operation and ends a half hour before it next begins operation.
The pupils of the school the zone serves are in class at the observation.
The stretch of highway at the observation lies within territory classed as a business district or as a residence district.
The road user's vehicle cannot be moved from the place where it stands at the observation, by its own power or otherwise.
The road user is required to be halted where it is at the observation by a legal duty other than the direction of an officer or a traffic-control device.
The underside of the road user's vehicle touches, or lacks the clearance to pass over, the surface it is travelling across at the observation.
